newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Troubled Lithuanian state bank gets new capital.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Lithuanian state bank gets new capital.

text.p: Lithuania's troubled State Commercial Bank has registered some $165 million of new capital, that will be bought by the government as a key plank of its rescue plan, bank officials said on Tuesday.

"The nominal value of each share is 100 litas and all of the shares will bought by the government," a bank spokesman told Reuters. The shares have been registered by the securities commission and will be registered by the central bank Thursday.
The government decided to recapitalise the bank, the largest bank in the country, after bad loans pushed it to the brink of insolvency.
The government acted swiftly to prevent a new wave of panic after Lithuania was struck by a crisis at two of its top commercial banks in December last year.
Some 155 million litas of the new capital is made up of government securities and the rest is budget cash.
